'''Business and economy'''
*[[Tariffs in the second Trump administration]]
**[[South Korea–United States relations]]
***[[South Korea]] announces it has finalized a trade deal with the [[United States]] in which the U.S. agrees to 15% of tariffs on imported South Korean goods and South Korea will invest in American businesses and shipbuilding projects. [https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/29/us/politics/tariff-trump-south-korea-trade.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least nine people are killed and five others are missing due to floods in [[central Vietnam|central]] [[Vietnam]], including in major cities such as [[Da Nang|Đà Nẵng]] and [[Hội An (city)|Hội An]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/floods-kill-4-leave-5-missing-central-vietnam-2025-10-29/ (Reuters)]

*The roof of the girls’ dormitory at a ''[[pesantren]]'' collapses due to heavy rain and strong winds in [[Situbondo]], [[East Java]], [[Indonesia]], killing a student and injuring 19 others. '''International relations'''
*[[Afghanistan–Pakistan relations]]
**[[2025 Afghanistan–Pakistan conflict]] 
***Peace talks held in [[Istanbul]], [[Turkey]], between [[Afghanistan]] and [[Pakistan]] collapse and achieve no clear agreement. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/afghanistan-pakistan-peace-talks-failed-pakistan-minister-says-2025-10-28/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Pelicot rape case]]
**The [[Senate (France)|French Senate]] approves amendments to [[France|the country]]'s [[Rape in France|rape law]] to include a [[Sexual consent in law|consent]]-based definition, clarifying that consent must be freely given and cannot be implied by silence or lack of resistance. [https://www.reuters.com/world/france-revamps-rape-law-after-gisele-pelicot-case-2025-10-29/ (Reuters)]
*[[Philippines|Philippine]] [[President of the Philippines|president]] [[Bongbong Marcos]] signs a [[Philippine legal codes|law]] institutionalizing a ban on the country's [[Philippine offshore gaming operator|offshore gaming operators]] and declaring their operations illegal. [https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1262062 (Philippine News Agency)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Alberta teachers' strike]]
**In the [[Canada|Canadian]] province of [[Alberta]], [[Premier of Alberta|premier]] [[Danielle Smith]] says legislation has been passed to end the strike, invoking the [[Section 33 of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms|notwithstanding clause]] to prevent court challenges of the legislation's constitutionality. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/alberta-teachers-back-to-work-bill-9.6955558 (CBC)] [https://globalnews.ca/news/11497842/alberta-passes-bill-end-teacher-strike/ (Global News)]
*[[2025 Dutch general election]]
**In the [[Netherlands]], a [[2025 Dutch general election|snap election]] is held following the collapse of the [[Schoof cabinet]] in June. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/oct/28/netherlands-polls-geert-wilders-faces-political-isolation (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Centrism|Centrist]] [[Social liberalism|liberal]] party [[Democrats 66]], led by [[Rob Jetten]], takes a surprise lead according to the main exit poll, just two years after the party ranked sixth in the previous vote. [https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/10/29/netherlands-national-elections-2025-the-results-in-pictures (''Euronews'')]
**[[Frans Timmermans]], the leader of the [[GroenLinks–PvdA]] alliance, steps down following a poor performance during the election. [https://www.politico.eu/article/frans-timmermans-quits-as-dutch-center-left-boss-after-election-debacle/ (''Politico'')]
*[[2025 Tanzanian general election]]
**[[Tanzanian]]s vote to elect a [[President of Tanzania|president]], members of the [[National Assembly (Tanzania)|National Assembly]], and [[Subdivisions of Tanzania|ward]] councillors. Incumbent president [[Samia Suluhu Hassan]] runs unopposed after the [[High Court of Tanzania|High Court]] barred main opposition leaders from participating in the elections. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2025/10/29/tanzania-election-president-samia-suluhu-hassan-opposition/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2025 Tanzanian election protests]]
**Protests and riots erupts in [[Dar es Salaam]] over electoral reforms and demands for free political activity, with demonstrators setting fire to vehicles and damaging public infrastructure. [[Tanzania Police Force|Tanzanian police]] use [[tear gas]] to break up the protests and impose a [[curfew]]. [[Internet in Tanzania|Internet connectivity]] is disrupted shortly after. [https://apnews.com/article/tanzania-election-samia-suluhu-hassan-d897483abe5a34c1b02422e7adc5891a (AP)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/oct/29/tanzania-election-president-samia-suluhu-hassan-poised-to-retain-power (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/tanzania-declares-curfew-commercial-capital-after-election-protests-2025-10-29/ (Reuters)]
